title: x11, asterix, erf: Delay field registration
description:
Asterix, X11, and ERF all register a large number of entries in the gpa_name_map GHashTable (currently 10124, 8328, and 5790, respectively), which takes a significant amount of time at initial startup for TShark. All of them register only fields with the same prefix as the protocol, and have common entry points into dissection, allowing delayed registration to occur upon dissection. (Other protocols with lots of registration time either register additional handoffs based on configuration files, like XML, or have many entry points that require lots of possible places to force registration, like nr-rrc, lte-rrc, and rrc.)

In addition, note that GHashTable, unlike some implementations, has no facility to reserve a certain amount of space and so does a moderately expensive copying of the table each time it reaches 15/16 capacity when adding fields. Since the capacity is always a power of 2, this means that one such expansion and copying occurs at 15*2^14=245760 entries. Not counting Diameter and RADIUS (which are already delayed registration due to reading from text configuration files), there are approximately 252166 fields (depending on the number of columns) in the hash table currently, but only 227924 with this change. That means that an initial GHashTable doubling and copy is saved.

This saves, according to callgrind, cachegrind, and real world testing, a little over 10% of time to run `tshark -r test/captures/empty.pcap` due to decreased startup time. It's a fairly small savings in absolute terms, but adds up over running TShark many times over a lot of (possibly small) files.

notes.body: Would it be useful to do a hastable implementation(add to the glib one) with the possibility to pre set size and possible the extension factor. Maybe a glib mr.

They have a really old, closed, unimplemented issue for it - https://gitlab.gnome.org/GNOME/glib/-/issues/12

Where they closed it a couple of years ago saying that no one had asked for in a decade since the original person.

I don't have an account on their GitLab, I recall at one point when I tried they made it somewhat difficult to get an account because of an influx of spam (maybe especially from GMail accounts.)
We also could implement the minimum capacity on wmem_map and switch to using that in epan scope.

I can add a comment to the GLib issue, but I'm not sure if our data point would warrant significant work on their part. It probably makes more sense to use wmem_map since it's something we directly control.

It also might be useful to look at using a more modern hashing algorithm for wmem_strong_hash such as xxHash.

commits_data.title: Asterix: delay field registration
commits_data.message:
Asterix: delay field registration

The Asterix dissector registers 10124 header_field_info and expert_info,
all of which have a common prefix "asterix," and there is a common entry
point into the dissector. Thus we can safely delay registration of
fields in order to hasten startup (especially on TShark.)

commits_data.title: X11: Delay field registration
commits_data.message:
X11: Delay field registration

The X11 dissector registers 8328 header_field_info and expert_info,
all of which have the "x11." prefix, and has only a single entry
point. Therefore we can safely delay registration of the fields in
order to hasten startup (especially on TShark.)

commits_data.title: erf: Delay field registration
commits_data.message:
erf: Delay field registration

The ERF dissector registers 5790 header_field_info and expert_info,
all beginning with the "erf." prefix, and has a single entry point to
the dissector. Thus, we can safely delay registering the fields under
the prefix to improve startup time (especially on TShark.)
